clue.text: Sees term out, academic term

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serves out the full length of their academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-year teaching period at a college or university, especially in the US, is a straightforward synonym for one academic term.

clue.text: Venomous creature in house? Any number

parts.note: in astrology each sign of the zodiac is linked to a house; Scorpio is one sign
N is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A poisonous creature could be lurking in any number of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests a building, but it is an astrological house, a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An arachnid with a stinging tail is a well-known example of a venomous creature.

clue.text: Stingy hoarder may cause endless grief

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: misery is grief or suffering

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted collector of money can cause no end of sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hoards wealth and spends as little as possible is the standard definition of the word.

clue.text: Arab in rush to be admitted to hospital

indicators.note: admitted to means taken inside, so the rush word goes into the hospital word

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
to race is to rush

explanation.surface: An Arab man is rushed into hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval Christians used this name for Arabs or Muslims, especially at the time of the Crusades.

clue.text: Some ordered a mozzarella cheese

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner ordered a mozzarella cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating is an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Criminal gang, Italian

parts.note: a gang is a band of people
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian (as in gin and it, Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A description of an Italian criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw or robber, the noun sense of a criminal, is a synonym.

clue.text: Musical instruction from an eminent Florentine

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, the poet of the Divine Comedy, was a famous native of Florence

explanation.surface: A distinguished Florentine gives a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian tempo marking meaning at a moderate walking pace, so a musical instruction.

clue.text: Tea missed abroad? Small cup of coffee provided

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abroad misses tea but is given a little coffee instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A French term for a small cup of strong black coffee, literally half-cup.

clue.text: Verbal onslaught from one stuck in traffic

indicators.note: stuck in means the one letter is lodged inside the traffic word

parts.note: traffic as in commerce is trade
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A furious rant from a driver stuck in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests road vehicles, but it is the commerce sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, angry speech of criticism is a verbal onslaught, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Watchful attendant behind old boy

indicators.note: behind places the attendant piece after the old boy piece in the answer

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school
an attendant is a servant

explanation.surface: A vigilant servant stands behind a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert and quick to notice things is a synonym pairing with watchful.

clue.text: He paints eccentric theatrical type

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric painter who is also something of a showman.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor, after Thespis, said to be the first Greek actor, is a theatrical type.

clue.text: Slightly reduced, modest object

indicators.note: a slight reduction means losing just one letter, here the last of the synonym

parts.note: modest and demure both describe a reserved, shy manner

explanation.surface: Something made a little smaller is now a modest object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, meaning to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection or show reluctance is the verb sense of object, a synonym.

clue.text: Page one — vulgar infringement of copyright

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
racy means risque or vulgar

explanation.surface: A tabloid's front page is flagged for crude plagiarism.
explanation.definitionFit: Unauthorised copying of protected work, such as films or software, is commonly called this, borrowing the word for robbery at sea.

clue.text: One feeding ruminants, back together again following separation

indicators.note: feeding here means going into the other piece, so one sits inside the other
back says the word for the ruminants is read the other way round

parts.note: deer are cud-chewing animals, ruminants
a unit is a single one

explanation.surface: Someone feeding grazing animals finds them back together after being parted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' here is a four-letter word rather than the usual I; 'back' gives REED, and the comma hides that 'back' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A family or couple brought back into union after a time apart is the plain sense of the clue phrase.

clue.text: Much less left by Greek character, single

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lone means single

explanation.surface: A single Greek, left behind and alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning not to mention or still less, used after a negative, as in can't walk, much less run.

clue.text: Wild rose experts in train

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rose specialists aboard a train going wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous luxury long-distance service between Paris and Istanbul is a specific example of a train.

clue.text: Kind heart unfortunately uninformed

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted person sadly left without information.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for knowing nothing about a matter, left unaware, matches uninformed.

clue.text: Ship's doctor eating last of succulent fish

indicators.note: eating means the doctor word takes the other letter inside it

parts.note: the medical officer on a ship is called the surgeon

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The ship's doctor dines on a juicy fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fish whose roe is caviar is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Accept a less important role and shock bench, perhaps

parts.note: to shock someone is to take them aback
a bench is an example of a seat, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone accepting a junior role is shocked by the bench they are given.
explanation.definitionFit: To step back from leadership and let others decide is the meaning of this common idiom about sitting behind.

clue.text: Stewed neck, hit in cookhouse

indicators.note: stewed means cooked and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stewed neck meat is a hit in the army canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where food is prepared and cooked is a synonym of cookhouse.

clue.text: Important bridge player leaving place in Florida

parts.note: key means important
the four players in bridge are named North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A key bridge player departs for somewhere in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: The southernmost city of the Florida Keys, a specific place in the state.

clue.text: Furtive type in frame after end of review

indicators.note: after places the frame word following the picked letter
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an easel is a frame that holds a painting

explanation.surface: A sneaky character gets into the picture after a review ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, deceitful person is figuratively called after the small predatory animal, a furtive type.

clue.text: Choice, but no starter choice

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a selection is a choice

explanation.surface: A menu where you may choose anything but a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' suggests a first course, but here it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote in which a candidate is chosen is a formal act of choice, a synonym.

clue.text: Odd story about eastern shellfish

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the anagram goes around the other letter
odd means strange, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange tale about some eastern seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges STORY into OYSTR, which goes 'about' E.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve mollusc prized for food and pearls is an example of shellfish.

clue.text: Article secured by the old clan chief

indicators.note: secured by means held inside, so the article goes within the other word

parts.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A document fastened by the former chief of a clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a document or item, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scotland, a nobleman who headed a clan or held land from the king held this title.

clue.text: Bird, female bird of prey

parts.note: an owl is a nocturnal bird of prey

explanation.surface: A female raptor is described as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A domesticated bird such as a chicken, or birds in general, is a synonym of bird.

clue.text: Male in band gets break

indicators.note: in places the male letter inside the band word

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder

explanation.surface: A man in a pop group gets his lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group, but it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter something into pieces is to break it, a synonym verb.

clue.text: Absolve former partner facing single charge

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
single means one
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: Someone forgives an ex-partner who faces a single criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame or guilt is a synonym of absolve.

clue.text: Latin ruler capturing island brings pleasure

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A Latin monarch takes an island and enjoys it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness or enjoyment of something is a synonym of pleasure, as in to one's taste.

clue.text: Nurse bringing in coffee for slovenly woman

indicators.note: bringing in means the nurse letters take the coffee inside them

parts.note: SRN stands for State Registered Nurse, a former British nursing qualification
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A nurse brings coffee to an untidy woman.
explanation.walkthrough: State Registered Nurse was a former British nursing qualification, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned derogatory word for a dirty, untidy woman, matching the clue phrase directly.
